questions.q: What is a reference field in ServiceNow?
options: A field that stores a copy of text from another table
A field on one table that points to a specific record on another table — ServiceNow's version of a foreign key
A field that can only ever point to the sys_user table
A field used exclusively for calculated numeric totals
questions.explain: A reference field holds a pointer to a specific record elsewhere, the same role a foreign key plays in a relational database.

questions.q: What is actually stored in incident.caller_id, even though the form displays a person's full name?
options: The person's full name as plain text
The person's email address
Nothing is stored until the form is submitted
The sys_id of the referenced sys_user record
questions.explain: The field stores the sys_id of the referenced record; the displayed name is a live lookup against that record's display value.

questions.q: Why does the name shown on caller_id update automatically if that person's name changes in sys_user?
options: A scheduled job rewrites every incident's caller_id field overnight
It doesn't update automatically; every incident must be edited by hand
Because caller_id only stores a pointer (sys_id), not the name itself — changing the referenced record changes what's displayed everywhere it's referenced
ServiceNow deletes and recreates the incident record
questions.explain: Since the stored value is a pointer, not text, the displayed value is always a fresh lookup of the current referenced record.

questions.q: What does the info icon next to a set reference field do?
options: It deletes the reference
It converts the reference field into a plain text field
It only appears on the sys_user table
It opens a preview of the referenced record (such as email or department) without navigating away from the current form
questions.explain: The preview icon lets you glance at the referenced record's details inline, since the field itself holds only a pointer, not those details.

questions.q: What is a related list, relative to a reference field?
options: The same relationship read in the reverse direction — records on another table that point back at the current record
An unrelated feature with no connection to reference fields
A list of every field defined on the current table
A list that only shows historical, deleted records
questions.explain: A related list shows the reverse direction of a reference relationship, such as every incident where a given user is the caller_id.
